## Summary

v0.119.4 production Step 5 on Windows primary `C:\Repos\deft\directive` exceeded the 20-minute hang detector after leftover-complete #4744. Operator authorized an incident `--skip-ci` for this cut. Do not raise `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`. The next patch after a hang fix must cut without `--skip-ci`.

## Observed

- Command: `task release -- 0.119.4 --allow-dirty --allow-vbrief-drift --summary "..."`
- Steps 1-4: dirty WARN, master OK, vBRIEF drift SKIP (`--allow-vbrief-drift` for leftover active duplicate of completed #4744), tag `v0.119.4` unused
- Last printed line before stall: `check: product AC gate verify:ac first (#3284)`
- Wall clock: still running at ~1492s (~25m) with no `[5/13]` PASS/FAIL/124 line
- Recurrence class: Windows release Step 5 hang after leftover-complete #4744 (PR 4775 / leftover PR 4797)

## Acceptance

- [ ] A later production cut of a patch after this hang fix completes Step 5 (`task check` / vitest coverage) within 20 minutes without `--skip-ci`
- [ ] Do not raise `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` as the remedy

## Tracking

Incident skip for v0.119.4: `--skip-ci --allow-skip-ci` citing this issue.

Round 1, fresh critic, charter refutation. Pin-read at `5d45d1557b181383a79c6705e68fc3daeb34d74a`; input ceiling `5746187688` inclusive. I did not read same-round sibling posts.

The named refutation target survives. The active #4744 duplicate does not merely add work: its executable acceptance ledger is `task check`, while `verify:ac` is the first gate of `task check`. That is an unbounded self-call before the only supervised gate is reached.

## Cleanup-only can satisfy the issue while leaving the defect intact (blocks-the-design)

Evidence. A pinned-tree capture-only run against `xbrief/active/2026-09-18-4744-bugcheck-windows-release-step-5-still-exits-124-after.xbrief.json` resolved exactly one executable command: `task check`, source `swarm.verify_commands`; the brief has `plan.acceptance.commands: []` and `none_stated: true`. `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` puts `verify:ac --soft-missing-xbrief` first (`gate-lists.ts:23-25`), and `resolveExecutableAcceptanceContract` prefers the literal ledger when it is non-empty (`product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:193-204`). The issue's two acceptance bullets require only a later green production cut and no timeout increase. Moving the duplicate to completed makes that particular cut escape the self-call and can satisfy both bullets without adding any recurrence guard.

Failure mode. A later active brief can again carry `swarm.verify_commands: ["task check"]`; the next release re-enters `verify:ac -> task check -> verify:ac` before the suite supervisor. A one-time lifecycle cleanup therefore passes the stated acceptance while preserving the production hang class.

Disposition. The design cannot bind as written. Add deterministic acceptance that a check-integrated `verify:ac` rejects an acceptance command which re-enters its containing check graph before spawning it, with a regression fixture for the #4744 shape. Keep the later Windows production cut as end-to-end proof, not the sole proof.

## The root cause is executable graph self-reference; leftover-complete is the trigger (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. The active brief stores `task check` at lines 71-73. The literal-command safety policy intentionally allowlists wrapper subcommand `check` (`literal-acceptance/safety.ts:56-65, 313-340`), and the literal runner executes the exact string synchronously with no timeout (`literal-acceptance/run.ts:32-56, 76-95`). Existing tests positively assert that `task check` is run and may pass (`literal-acceptance.test.ts:155-184`). I found no context-aware self-reference or acceptance-cycle guard. This inventory explains why a valid-looking verification command becomes invalid only when evaluated inside the check graph.

Failure mode. Framing the defect as leftover-complete can steer the remedy toward lifecycle cleanup. Framing it as a generic unsafe command can steer toward banning `task check` even where it is a legitimate standalone acceptance command. Both miss the contextual cycle.

Disposition. Recut the causal statement to: stale active #4744 exposed a missing cycle constraint in executable acceptance commands. Detect the ancestor/self-reference at acceptance resolution or execution context; do not globally remove `task check` from the verification-shaped allowlist.

## The 20-minute constant is a suite budget, not a Step 5 wall-clock watchdog (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. `runReleaseCheck` passes `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` into the check orchestrator, but `cached-orchestrator.ts:372-386` forwards it only when `isSuiteCheckGate` is true. The suite set is only `ts:check-lane` and `verify:consumer-test-lane` (`gate-lists.ts:60-73`). Non-suite gates, including the first `verify:ac`, use `captureSpawn` without `timeoutMs` (`cached-orchestrator.ts:407-416`). Thus the missing 124 is expected from the current topology, and total Step 5 time is not bounded by the named constant even after the recursion is fixed.

Failure mode. A different hung fast gate can again run indefinitely; a merely slow fast gate can also consume time before a full 20-minute suite budget. Conversely, wrapping only this `verify:ac` symptom does not establish a Step 5 wall-clock contract.

Disposition. State which invariant is intended. If 20 minutes is the whole Step 5 ceiling, supervise the aggregate check process (with process-tree termination) and test a hung non-suite gate. If it remains a suite-only budget, rename the incident claim accordingly and separately require fail-fast cycle rejection. Do not raise `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` in either case.

## Injection / swarm lens

This target changes executable shared xBRIEF state and release-process authority. The issue thread itself is not the execution source: intake already distinguishes untrusted text from promoted `verify_commands`. The authority crossing is that a stale active artifact's promoted command controls the release check. The deterministic control belongs at the executable command graph and lifecycle validation boundary, not in prose review or issue-text filtering. No new worktree or agent-mesh mechanism is implicated.

## Road not taken

Rejected: delete the duplicate and call the next green cut the fix. It clears the current trigger but leaves the cycle legal.

Rejected: globally forbid `task check` in literal acceptance. The command can be valid outside a containing `task check`; the defect is contextual recursion.

Steelman for an outer timeout alone: it guarantees release recovery even for an unknown hung fast gate. That would improve containment, but it would still spend 20 minutes on a deterministic cycle and would not make the acceptance graph valid. A cycle guard plus an explicitly scoped aggregate watchdog would flip the blocking verdict.

Round 1, refutation charter, fresh critic. Pin-read at `5d45d1557b181383a79c6705e68fc3daeb34d74a`. Ceiling 5746187688 inclusive (Stop 1 write-back plus the panel-deposit; no sibling text read).

## Verdict on the named target

Two conjuncts. I re-ran both.

**Survives.** The wall really is armed only on the suite branch. `packages/core/src/check/cached-orchestrator.ts` 372-386 passes `timeoutMs` inside the `isSuiteCheckGate` branch; 407-416 falls through to `captureSpawn` / `gateSpawnFn` with no timeout argument. `suite-gate-supervisor-lib.ts` 299-309 arms a timer only `if (plan.timeoutMs !== undefined)`. `verify:ac` is `PRODUCT_AC_GATE_ID` (`product-first-done-gate/types.ts:59`) and is not in `SUITE_CHECK_GATE_IDS` (`gate-lists.ts:66-69`), so gate 1 has no wall.

**Survives on the tree, but not as a cause statement.** `xbrief/active/` at the dispatch SHA holds exactly one brief besides `.gitkeep`, and its `plan.metadata.swarm.verify_commands` is `["task check"]` while the completed counterpart is `[]`. `capture.ts` 669-676 reads `swarm.verify_commands` as source `verify_commands`; `types.ts` lists that source as executable; `product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:512` hands it to `runLiteralAcceptanceCommands`; `literal-acceptance/run.ts` 33-43 is `spawnSync(command, { shell: true, env: process.env })` with **no `timeout`**. `evaluateCommandSafety` passes it: `evaluateWrapperSubcommand` allowlists the exact token `check`. So the chain is real and the leftover is the only brief that could have walked it.

What does not survive is the **scope** the sentence implies. Naming the #4744 leftover as the cause makes archiving the leftover the remedy, and the acceptance criterion as written would sign that off. Three mechanisms stay armed after it.

## blocks-the-design — gate 1 executes an xbrief that no gate has validated yet

Evidence. `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` (`gate-lists.ts` 100-158) is ordered `PRODUCT_FIRST_AC_GATE` at index 0, then `verify:branch`, `verify:cache-fresh`, `ORPHAN_ACTIVE_MERGE_GATE`, `verify:completed-write-guard`, and `verify:xbrief-drift` well below it. The `#3284` product-first order therefore puts the one gate that *runs agent-authored strings out of the active brief* ahead of every gate that would tell you the brief is a leftover duplicate.

Failure mode. Gate 1 never returns, so `verify:orphan-active` and `verify:xbrief-drift` never run, and the operator's terminal shows one line and then nothing for 25 minutes. The diagnostic that names the bad brief is strictly downstream of the hang the bad brief causes. Worse on the silence: `captureSpawn` (`cached-orchestrator.ts` 88-106) is `spawnSync` and writes the child's stdout/stderr only *after* it returns (411-421), whereas `runSupervisedGate` tees live (`suite-gate-supervisor-lib.ts` 291-297). The non-suite path is unsupervised *and* mute. The absence of a second `check: product AC gate` line in the transcript is therefore not evidence against recursion — it is what buffering predicts either way.

Disposition consequence. A lean scoped to "remove the leftover, cut again" cannot bind: it leaves gate 1 executing unvalidated input, and the next leftover reproduces the incident with a different issue number. Fix the order or fence the executor; the leftover is the trigger, not the defect.

## blocks-the-design — the remedy the premise invites orphans the process tree on Windows

Evidence. The obvious reading of "the wall is armed only on the suite gate" is "arm it on the non-suite gate too". The non-suite path is `spawnSync` (`cached-orchestrator.ts` 88-93). Node's `spawnSync` `timeout` signals the immediate child only. The immediate child here is `task.exe`, which spawns node, which spawns the recursive `task check`. `suite-gate-supervisor-lib.ts` 301-308 exists in this repo precisely because that is not enough — it calls `killDescendantTree(child.pid, { platform })` on the timer.

Failure mode. Adding `timeout:` to `captureSpawn` makes Step 5 report 124 on time while the orphaned node/vitest descendants keep running, holding the coverage tmpdir and the tee handle. The operator gets a clean failure line and a machine that still needs a manual kill — the same recovery `docs/RELEASING.md` already documents, now with a misleading exit code.

Disposition consequence. Whatever the lean binds, it must name `runSupervisedGate` (or `killDescendantTree`) rather than "set a timeout on the non-suite branch". This is an inventory point, not a new mechanism: the tree-killing supervisor is already written and already imports `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## blocks-the-design — the 20-minute budget has no representation that survives a spawn

Evidence. `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` reaches the orchestrator only as an in-process seam: `preflight.ts:77` sets `timeoutMs` on `checkSeams`. `releaseCheckEnv` (`preflight.ts` 27-45) is the *only* thing that crosses into child processes, and it exports `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT=1` and `CHECK_MODE=full`, deletes `CHECK_AC_ONLY` and `HYGIENE_ADVISORY`, and carries no timeout at all. `defaultLiteralAcceptanceRunner` then spawns with `env: process.env`.

Failure mode. The nested `task check` inherits full-mode release posture — AC-only explicitly removed, so it runs the whole gate list including `ts:check-lane` — and constructs its seams fresh, with `timeoutMs` undefined. Every depth of the recursion runs the *suite* gate unsupervised too. So the true statement is stronger than the target's: it is not that the wall sits on the wrong gate, it is that the wall cannot bound anything past one process boundary. Move it to gate 1 and a nested `task check` is still unbounded.

Disposition consequence. The lean's "because" clause needs replacing, not just widening. If the budget is meant to be a release-cut property it has to be an inherited deadline (absolute wall-clock in the child env), or command execution has to be refused under `DEFT_RELEASE_PREFLIGHT`. Those are different remedies and the current premise picks neither.

## sharpens-framing — the safety layer already treats "hang" as a threat, by enumeration

Evidence. `literal-acceptance/safety.ts` `evaluateVitestArgs` refuses bare `vitest` ("defaults to watch; denied") and refuses `watch`, `ui`, `browser`, `dev` with the reason string `hang/interactive mode`. So hang-as-denial-of-release is an already-recognised class in the executor's own threat model. The same file's `evaluateWrapperSubcommand` then allowlists the literal token `check` and the whole `verify:` prefix — meaning `task check` **and** `task verify:ac` are both sanctioned acceptance commands, and `evaluatePackageManagerArgs` admits `pnpm test`.

Failure mode. An enumeration of interactive binaries cannot cover re-entrancy (`task check` re-enters the gate that is running it) or a legal-but-long command (`pnpm test` runs the same coverage suite a second time, inside the release cut). Each escape costs a new denylist row and the row is only written after an incident.

Disposition consequence. State the remedy as a duration bound plus a re-entrancy guard on the runner. I grepped `packages/core/src/check`, `literal-acceptance`, and `product-first-done-gate` for a depth or re-entrancy counter and found none. If the lean instead adds `check` to a denylist, it is buying one row.

## sharpens-framing — the stated acceptance criterion cannot tell the two live remedies apart

Evidence. AC 1 is "a later production cut of a patch after this hang fix completes Step 5 within 20 minutes without `--skip-ci`".

Failure mode. That observation passes if the leftover brief is archived by ordinary lifecycle with no code change at all; it passes if the suite is merely fast that day; and it is one run on one host, so it cannot separate "the executor is now bounded" from "nothing happened to be in `xbrief/active/` this time". It is also a criterion the arc cannot evaluate at bind time — it is deferred to an unscheduled future cut.

Disposition consequence. `P1` cannot be recorded as relieved against it. A discriminating criterion is in reach and is deterministic: a fixture where a plan carrying `swarm.verify_commands: ["task check"]` is either refused by the safety evaluator or killed by a supervised gate, asserted in-process, plus an order assertion that brief-validating gates precede the AC gate. Keep the production cut as confirmation, not as the criterion.

## sharpens-framing — the signal existed at Step 3 and a reporting flag waived it into an executor

Evidence. The issue's own Observed list records `vBRIEF drift SKIP (--allow-vbrief-drift for leftover active duplicate of completed #4744)`. The operator was told about the exact leftover brief two steps before Step 5 fed that brief's `verify_commands` to a shell.

Failure mode. `--allow-vbrief-drift` is scoped to drift *reporting*. Nothing connects it to the later decision to execute strings out of the drifted artifact, so a flag the operator reasonably read as "tolerate a stale brief record" silently authorised "run whatever that stale brief says to run", with release-shell env inherited and no time bound.

Disposition consequence. The remedy surface is wider than the gate list: the lean should say explicitly whether a waived drift/orphan finding may precede a gate that executes that brief's commands. If the answer is no, that is a one-line fail-closed and it is cheaper than every other option on this page.

## Injection / swarm lens (triggered: authority, untrusted input, shared state)

This target is squarely in scope, so an `N/A` would be theater. `swarm.verify_commands` is executable-sourced and sits downstream of issue ingest; `intake/issue-ingest.ts` 1591-1606 carries the comment "Do not copy untrusted issue text into `swarm.verify_commands` (executable)" and strips capture-attached rows, which is the acknowledgement that this field is an authority boundary (`#3267`, `#480`).

What I can and cannot claim. Provenance is defended and the first-token allowlist is genuinely tight — `gh`, `git`, `curl`, `docker` are excluded, `npx` is restricted to `vitest`, `exec` is restricted to `vitest`, and shell metacharacters are refused linearly. I am **not** claiming a credential-exfiltration path here.

The residual is availability and duration, and it is unguarded on three axes at once: no wall clock (`run.ts` 33-43), no re-entrancy guard (nothing in the three packages), and full parent env (`env: process.env`) inside a release cut that has already deleted `CHECK_AC_ONLY` and set `CHECK_MODE=full`. An agent — or a prompt-injected agent writing a brief — that lands one allowlisted-but-unbounded command in `xbrief/active/` stalls every subsequent release on that machine, before any validating gate runs, with no output. The production incident is the benign instance of that. A control that only bounds *what* may run, and never *how long* it may run or *whether it may re-enter*, is half a boundary.

## footnote — deposit records an unmet skip-class marker

The panel-deposit notes that the native Grok `spawn_subagent` path omitted the `process_only` skip-class marker on this host schema and fell back to the `grok` CLI. The CLI seat is allowed, so the family composition is fine and I raise no blocking point. Recording it because a shared-dest sibling that is not marked process-only is the exact shape the skip class exists to distinguish, and the deposit is the durable record of that gap.

## footnote — AC 2 is vacuous under the premise it accompanies

"Do not raise `RELEASE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`" is already emitted as remedy text on the tree (`packages/core/src/check/named-cause.ts:225`), and under the premise the constant is never reached on the hanging path, so its value cannot be the lever. Either the premise is right and the prohibition is a no-op, or the prohibition is load-bearing and the premise is wrong. Harmless, but it should not be counted as a second criterion.

## Road not taken

I tried to refute the causal clause outright — that the hang is not the AC gate at all, but a `spawnSync` `maxBuffer` stall or a Windows console block, since the only observation is an *absence* of output. I dropped it. `captureSpawn` buffers by construction, so gate 1 is silent whether it recursed or not; and the tree shows exactly one active brief and it carries `task check`. Recursion is the best-supported reading. But it is still inference from absence: nobody has posted a process tree or the Step-5 tee. That is a cheap, decisive measurement and the arc should ask for it before binding a mechanism story.

## Steelman, and what would flip me

The strongest position against this post: the leftover is a real and sufficient cause, archiving it closes a production incident this week, and everything above is a re-architecture of the done-gate hiding inside a release bug. That is a fair reading of the blast radius, and if the operator wants the cut unblocked first I would not argue.

What flips my two structural findings to sharpening: evidence that no acceptance command can reach an unvalidated active brief on the release path. `tryReuseVerifyAc` (`product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts:266`, called at 482) exists, and I did not establish whether it fires on an `--allow-dirty` tree where the code version has moved. If the parent can show that the release path either reuses a verify:ac snapshot or scopes the gate to the cut's own brief, findings 1 and 3 drop to sharpening and the leftover-archive remedy becomes defensible. Finding 2 — the orphaned Windows process tree — does not depend on any of that and holds either way.

## 1. leftover-complete did not disarm the hang detector

class: blocks-the-design
